filming.feedback: The abrupt head move appears as the swing starts. Slow that transition rather than trying to freeze your head for the whole rep.
filming.limits: A head trace is not eye tracking. Natural stride motion, pitch adjustment, and finish rotation remain permitted; an arbitrary two-inch box is not a universal standard.

drills.name: No-Swing Pitch Tracking
drills.objective: Separate ball observation and stance control from swinging.
drills.equipment: Helmet, protected consistent tosser, soft balls, net; no bat initially.
steps: Take a comfortable stance in a clear safe area.
Receive gentle predictable tosses without swinging or reaching to catch.
Attend to the ball from release into the receiving net.
After each toss, report a simple location such as high/middle/low.
Use 6–8 takes, then compare a short normal-swing set separately.

filming.views: Side plus protected face-visible view; head, torso, pelvis/feet, ball, release and zone reference.
filming.phase: Release → zone passage → report; no bat contact.
filming.review: Track visible head orientation/translation and stance recovery, comparing similar feeds. Score the stated location against labeled ball passage separately. A wrong call is a task outcome, not automatic evidence of poor balance or head motion.
filming.feedback: Keep a comfortable stance and make the location call after the ball passes.
filming.limits: The system cannot verify continuous gaze or perception from head pose. Flinching or an errant feed should prompt safety review, not a mechanical diagnosis.

drills.name: Color-Call Takes
drills.objective: Add an explicit recognition response while preserving comfortable head and body control.
drills.equipment: Soft training balls with large visible colors/marks, helmet, protected gentle tosser, net; no bat.
steps: Begin with slow, consistently delivered tosses and clearly distinguishable colors.
Take every toss without swinging or catching it.
Report the color after passage, without moving closer to the flight path.
Slow or simplify the feed if the marking is not reliably visible.
Complete 6–8 takes; score recognition separately from movement.

filming.views: Full-body plus clear ball view; ball identity, release, head/torso, feet.
filming.phase: Release → passage → report.
filming.review: Compare reported color with ground truth and count abstentions or unclear markings. Review lunging/ducking or recovery only as visible movement observations. Ensure color-label errors from the camera are not attributed to the hitter.
filming.feedback: Stay in the comfortable stance; if you cannot see the mark, say so and we will slow the toss.
filming.limits: Color calls do not measure gaze fixation, pitch-spin recognition, or visual acuity. Lighting, color-vision differences, and marking visibility can affect performance.

drills.name: Controlled Take-or-Swing Reads
drills.objective: Test control when the hitter must decide, not merely repeat a predetermined swing.
drills.equipment: Helmet, bat, soft balls, protected consistent tosser, net, agreed reachable target window.
steps: Agree on a simple comfortable swing window before the round.
Begin with predictable gentle feeds and a few clear takes outside that window.
Swing only at suitable feeds; take the others without a forced check swing.
Review the choice, body control, and contact outcome separately.
Use 6–8 deliveries, then a short matched normal-swing check if workload allows.

filming.views: Side plus protected oblique; head/torso, pelvis/feet, grip/bat, ball, release and target window.
filming.phase: Release → decision response → swing/contact or take → recovery.
filming.review: Label delivered location and actual swing/take before examining balance. Review repeated pre-contact head/torso surges with rushed footwork or recovery on comparable swing trials. Keep decision accuracy, head movement, contact, and balance in separate fields; use only swing trials for contact-based analysis.
filming.feedback: Make the same comfortable move and keep the option to take; do not rush just because the ball is coming.
filming.limits: A poor decision does not establish a head-control defect. Ordinary video cannot identify when the hitter perceived the pitch or diagnose anxiety, attention problems, or visual impairment.

drills.name: Paused Standing Scoop Toss
drills.objective: Rehearse a comfortable rear-side gather and coordinated release without added approach momentum.
drills.equipment: Coach-selected light medicine ball, approved wall/landing lane, flat non-slip surface, target marker.
steps: Stand side-on to the target with a comfortable base.
Hold the ball with both hands near the rear hip and make a small gather.
Pause briefly without sinking farther or twisting to end range.
Turn and scoop-release smoothly; allow natural foot motion and follow-through.
Let the ball stop, reset, and complete 4–6 total reps across comfortable directions.

filming.views: Side/oblique; hips, shoulders, rear knee/foot, hands, ball, head, target.
filming.phase: Gather → pause → turn → release → recovery.
filming.review: Verify the pause separately from throw quality. Review continued knee folding/pelvis descent followed by a rushed rise, or hand/ball travel that occurs with an abrupt torso correction. Compare matched paused throws, then assess normal swings independently.
filming.feedback: Use a smaller gather so you can turn and release without rising to recover.
filming.limits: A pause changes rhythm; throw speed/distance does not reveal rear-leg force or prove bat-speed improvement.

drills.name: Split-Stance Scoop Toss
drills.objective: Explore lead-side support and rotation from a pre-set staggered base.
drills.equipment: Light medicine ball, approved target area, floor marks, non-slip surface.
steps: Set the lead foot slightly closer to the target in a comfortable staggered stance.
Hold the ball near the rear hip; do not force a long split or locked front knee.
Make a small gather and rotate into a two-hand scoop release without adding a stride.
Allow a comfortable pivot and finish; stop if the feet slide.
Reset for 4–6 total throws, changing direction only after a safe setup.

filming.views: Side plus oblique; both feet/knees, pelvis, torso, hands, ball/target.
filming.phase: Pre-set stance → gather → release → finish; there is no new lead-foot landing.
filming.review: Review lead-knee folding together with continued pelvis travel and recovery, or deliberate knee lockout with a body jolt. Record an added step as compliance first, distinguishing a necessary safety recovery from intended foot release.
filming.feedback: Turn from the base you set rather than sliding forward through it.
filming.limits: A visible front-leg position does not measure braking force or weight transfer, and a stable bent knee is not a failed block.

drills.name: Step-Back Scoop Toss
drills.objective: Connect a small rearward step to a smooth forward/rotational transition.
drills.equipment: Light medicine ball, approved target lane, clear approach space, floor marks.
steps: Rehearse the footwork without a ball first.
Hold the ball comfortably and take a small rear-foot step away from the target along the intended movement line.
Gather, then move into a controlled lead-foot landing and turn.
Scoop-release without a hop or forced knee extension.
Wait for the ball to stop; complete 4–6 total throws, returning to #58 if control is poor.

filming.views: Wide side/oblique; both feet, rear knee/hip, pelvis, head/torso, hands, ball.
filming.phase: Rear step → gather → lead landing → release.
filming.review: Review an oversized step/hop with a rushed landing, or rear-side rise with a late arm correction. Compare against the same step-back task rather than penalizing intended rearward travel. Check ball position remains controllable during the approach.
filming.feedback: Shorten the backward step so the landing and release stay smooth.
filming.limits: This is a proposed combination, not a standard drill. Visible movement cannot establish pressure transfer, and added momentum must not be mistaken for greater intrinsic rotational power.

drills.name: Step-In Rotational Toss
drills.objective: Blend a short approach with a controlled plant, turn, and release.
drills.equipment: Light medicine ball, approved target/landing lane, approach marks, non-slip surface.
steps: Begin only a short comfortable step from the throwing setup.
Hold the ball securely and rehearse the approach at walking pace.
Step into the side-on release setup, receive the landing, then turn and throw.
Finish without a forced stop or running into the rebound lane.
Reset fully for 4–6 total throws; no run-up is required.

filming.views: Wide side plus oblique; both feet/knees, pelvis, torso/head, hands, ball/target.
filming.phase: Approach → landing → turn/release → recovery.
filming.review: Review continued forward collapse or foot sliding after landing with an awkward release/recovery. Separate the intended approach from unwanted post-landing travel; inspect whether the ball starts moving toward the target before a stable transition is established, without imposing a universal timing cutoff.
filming.feedback: Slow the step so you can turn from the landing instead of chasing the throw.
filming.limits: Approach speed changes output. A farther throw does not prove better front-leg bracing or improved hitting mechanics.

drills.name: Small-Shuffle Scoop Toss
drills.objective: Coordinate extra footwork, a rear-side gather, and a controlled release.
drills.equipment: Light medicine ball, approved target, clear non-slip lane, optional footfall marks.
steps: Rehearse a small sideways shuffle without crossing the feet.
Add the ball once the footwork is controlled.
Gather into the rear side, land on the lead side, and turn into the scoop throw.
Keep the approach modest; do not jump into release or chase a hard rebound.
Use 4–6 total throws with full resets, reverting to #61 or #58 if needed.

filming.views: Wide side/oblique; both feet, rear knee/hip, pelvis, torso/head, hands, ball.
filming.phase: Shuffle → gather → lead landing → release → recovery.
filming.review: Identify footfalls before judging timing. Review a hop, tangled feet, or stalled gather followed by a rushed arm throw and recovery. Distinguish planned approach steps from uncontrolled steps after release.
filming.feedback: Make the shuffle smaller so the gather and release stay connected.
filming.limits: This footwork adaptation is not a mandated swing pattern. Throw output cannot isolate rear-leg power, and different approach distances must not be pooled into one score.

drills.name: Step-Behind Rotational Push Throw
drills.objective: Explore a controlled step-behind approach to a rotational push once simpler throws are reliable.
drills.equipment: Light coach-selected medicine ball, approved target lane, ample clear space; direct supervision.
steps: Begin side-on with the ball near the rear shoulder, supported by both hands.
Rehearse a small rear-foot step behind the lead foot, then a lead-foot step toward the target.
Turn and push-release with the rear-side hand while the other hand guides safely.
Follow through comfortably without trapping or tangling the feet.
Allow the rebound to stop; use 4 total controlled throws or substitute #66.

filming.views: Side plus oblique; crossed-foot events, hips/shoulders, rear elbow/wrist, both hands, ball.
filming.phase: Cross-step → opening step → turn → release.
filming.review: Verify leg identity during crossing, then review foot tangling, late landing, abrupt torso correction, or uncomfortable-looking delivery that prompts the athlete to stop. Compare the shoulder-level push with shot-put references, not scoop trajectories.
filming.feedback: Remove the cross-step until you can land and release without tangling the feet.
filming.limits: Rebound catching is intentionally omitted. Do not infer shoulder loading, pain, or safe joint range from pose, and do not map a one-arm push directly to top-hand bat mechanics.

drills.name: Tall-Kneeling Rotational Scoop
drills.objective: Explore comfortable rotational delivery with stepping removed.
drills.equipment: Very light suitable ball, firm knee pad, approved target area, coach supervision.
steps: Kneel on both knees on the pad in a comfortable upright position.
Hold the ball in two hands and make a small comfortable turn to one side.
Rotate back toward the target and release gently without forcing a long backswing.
Allow comfortable hip/torso motion rather than pinning the pelvis.
Reset for 4 total throws across comfortable directions; choose standing work if kneeling is uncomfortable.

filming.views: Side/oblique; hips, shoulders, head, knees/pad, hands, ball.
filming.phase: Kneeling setup → gather → release → settle.
filming.review: Review uncontrolled leaning, rising off the pad, or a catch-up torso motion after the ball moves. Record pad/knee movement and recovery separately from the chosen torso pattern; there is no foot-stride event.
filming.feedback: Keep the turn within a comfortable range and use a lighter ball if you need to lean to release it.
filming.limits: Kneeling does not isolate one muscle group or prove core strength. A stable kneeling throw cannot establish lower-body sequencing in a normal swing.

drills.name: Half-Kneeling Scoop Toss
drills.objective: Review rotational control from an asymmetric supported base.
drills.equipment: Very light suitable ball, firm pad, approved target, non-slip floor.
steps: Place one knee on the pad and the other foot ahead in a comfortable stable position.
Start facing the target with the ball near the kneeling-side hip.
Make a modest gather, then rotate and scoop toward the target without striking the raised knee.
Reset fully; switch setup only when the ball is still.
Take 4 total reps, normally 2 per comfortable orientation, or return to standing if needed.

filming.views: Front/oblique plus side; lead foot/knee, kneeling knee/pad, hips/shoulders, head, hands, ball.
filming.phase: Setup → gather → release → recovery.
filming.review: Review lead-foot rocking/sliding, pelvis leaning, or a late arm lift to clear the leg. Tag which knee is down so mirrored views do not reverse the interpretation. A moving torso is expected; review control rather than enforcing a stationary pelvis.
filming.feedback: Adjust the setup so the ball clears your leg without a last-second lift or lean.
filming.limits: A knee-on-pad constraint changes the movement and may not suit the athlete. Camera projection does not diagnose hip mobility or determine a correct trunk-separation angle.

drills.name: Standing Rotational Push Throw
drills.objective: Coordinate a rotational push with the body turn and a controlled finish.
drills.equipment: Light suitable medicine ball, approved target/landing lane, non-slip ground.
steps: Stand side-on with the ball comfortably near the rear shoulder or upper chest.
Place the rear-side hand behind the ball and the other hand in support.
Make a small gather, rotate, and push-release toward a reachable target.
Do not force elbow lockout, wrist snap, or a high launch angle.
Reset for 4–6 total throws; reduce the load or return to a two-hand scoop if uncomfortable.

filming.views: Side/oblique; shoulders/hips, rear elbow/wrist, supporting hand, feet, head, ball.
filming.phase: Gather → turn → push/release → recovery.
filming.review: Review an early reach/push that accompanies limited torso movement and a late body correction relative to controlled same-task reps. Inspect abrupt leaning or foot recovery after release. Distinguish intentional elbow extension in a push from premature extension labels used in bat swings.
filming.feedback: Blend the body turn and the push instead of reaching first and catching up afterward.
filming.limits: Hand/arm force cannot be measured from this video. A rotational shot put is not a bat swing, and ball spin or flight alone cannot validate a kinetic-chain sequence.

drills.name: Half-Kneeling Rotational Push
drills.objective: Explore comfortable upper-body push timing with stepping removed.
drills.equipment: Very light suitable ball, firm knee pad, approved target area, supervision.
steps: Set a comfortable half-kneeling base facing the target.
Hold the ball near the rear-side shoulder with one hand behind and the other supporting.
Make a small turn and push-release without forcing a large twist.
Let the arms follow through and regain a comfortable base.
Complete 4 total throws or substitute #66 if kneeling is awkward.

filming.views: Side plus front/oblique; knees/foot/pad, hips/shoulders, both hands, rear elbow, ball, head.
filming.phase: Setup through release and recovery.
filming.review: Review torso side-fall, lead-foot sliding, or a late push after a balance correction. Track elbow extension as an intentional task feature, not an automatic “barring” fault. Record the actual kneeling orientation for matched comparisons.
filming.feedback: Use a smaller turn and lighter ball so the push does not pull you off the base.
filming.limits: This does not isolate the arms or establish top-hand strength. Pose cannot diagnose knee/shoulder stress, and visible compensations should prompt coaching review rather than a medical label.

drills.name: Controlled Overhead Floor Slam
drills.objective: Practice a controlled raise, downward release, and recovery as a general athletic task.
drills.equipment: Appropriately light low/no-bounce slam ball rated for floor impact, approved floor, clear space, supervision.
steps: Start with a comfortable stance and the ball supported in both hands.
Raise it only within a comfortable overhead range without forcing a back arch.
Use a controlled downward throw to a clear floor spot in front of, not under, the feet.
Keep clear of any rebound and wait until the ball stops before retrieval.
Perform 4 total slams; omit this drill if overhead movement or the facility setup is unsuitable.

filming.views: Side plus oblique; hands/ball, shoulders/hips, head, feet, floor target.
filming.phase: Raise → downward release → impact → recovery; ball impact is not hitter contact.
filming.review: Review abrupt backward lean during the raise, loss of support on release, unsafe foot proximity to the impact zone, or an uncontrolled attempt to catch a rebound. Expected downward torso motion is not a “posture collapse” by itself.
filming.feedback: Use a comfortable raise and place the slam safely ahead of your feet, then let the ball stop.
filming.limits: This is a general supplemental adaptation, not a hitting-specific mechanic or proof of front-leg blocking. Do not infer spinal loading from a torso line.

drills.name: Medicine-Ball Carry and Place
drills.objective: Practice approaching, decelerating, and intentionally placing an object while maintaining control.
drills.equipment: Manageable medicine ball, stable broad low platform appropriate to the athlete, non-slip lane, clear reset area.
steps: Pick up and hold the ball comfortably near the torso.
Walk a short marked path toward the platform; do not begin with a sprint.
Slow down and place the ball gently without dropping, throwing, or colliding with the platform.
Release only once the ball is supported, then step away.
Reset for 4 total placements; reduce load or distance if control deteriorates.

filming.views: Full-body side/oblique; feet, pelvis/torso/head, hands/ball, platform boundary.
filming.phase: Carry → approach/deceleration → placement → hand release → exit.
filming.review: Review extra recovery steps, a dropped ball, collision risk, or a rushed forward lean during placement. Confirm support before labeling a release successful; distinguish the intended placement bend from loss of posture.
filming.feedback: Slow earlier so you can place the ball rather than dropping it to catch your balance.
filming.limits: This is general movement control, not a direct batting drill. No ballistic release speed, swing-power score, or front-leg force can be inferred from completion time.

quickKey.text: Four drill task reps, then four normal two-hand swings. Remove the drill constraint for the normal swings.

quickKey.label: Session order
quickKey.text: Prepare → 6 baseline swings → optional focus block → rear-leg block → front-leg block → upper-body block → 6 uncued exit swings.

quickKey.label: Volume
quickKey.text: Base session = 36 task reps. Add ONE posture (P), balance/head-control (B), OR medicine-ball (M) block, 4 + 4, for 44 task reps. Dry rehearsals, takes, and throws count as task reps, not necessarily swings; log warm-up and extra tests separately.

quickKey.label: Reduced version
quickKey.text: 4 baseline → 2 + 2 per block → 4 exit = 20 task reps, or 24 with one focus block. For #3 use one dry rehearsal and one tee swing; for #21 use one two-swing pair.

quickKey.label: Controlled rep
quickKey.text: No slip or unplanned recovery, and the chosen movement issue is absent or improved against the coach-approved reference. Record contact quality separately; a hard hit alone is not a mechanical pass.

quickKey.label: Proposed advance rule
quickKey.text: At least 4 of 6 assessable normal exit swings controlled, no pain/new safety issue, and no material worsening from baseline; confirm with the next session's matched baseline. Reduced version: 3 of 4. These are coaching rules for this plan, not validated age-specific standards.

quickKey.label: Safety and video
quickKey.text: Scale to the hitter and total workload. Stop for pain, slipping, or unsafe bat control; never force a locked knee or rigid head. Use fixed full-body side video and a protected oblique view when available; uncertain footage is “not assessable,” not a failed rep.

quickKey.label: Medicine-ball kit
quickKey.text: Coach-selected manageable ball of known mass, approved throwing wall/landing area, non-slip floor, clear throw/rebound lane. A batting net is not assumed suitable. No rapid rebound catching; let the ball stop before retrieval, then clear the lane and rest as needed before normal swings.

quickKey.label: Medicine-ball count
quickKey.text: M means 4 throws TOTAL, normally 2 each comfortable direction, then 4 normal swings, not 4 throws per side. Reduced M = 2 throws total + 2 swings. Rehearsals count as extra; #58 can replace a harder M task at any stage.

quickKey.label: Medicine-ball review
quickKey.text: Observe release/recovery, not bat contact. Record ball mass/type and actual throws per direction; a successful throw does not prove hitting improvement or measure force/power.

stages.name: Gather, Land, Deliver

blocks.run: Small no-bat rear-hip hinge; brief hold; reset.
blocks.watch: Continued sinking plus an extra body/foot adjustment.

blocks.run: Stride without swinging; hold the comfortable landing about 2 seconds.
blocks.watch: Sliding or needing a recovery step.

blocks.run: Gentle top-hand-only tee swings; free hand on chest; restore two hands.
blocks.watch: Early reaching or elbow advancement with delayed barrel delivery.

focus.run: Small hinge → slow stride → comfortable landing hold.
Count load → stride → identify target → slow dry swing.
Small rear-hip gather, brief pause, smooth scoop throw; watch for sinking and a recovery rise.

stages.goal: Comfortable load, controlled landing, manageable barrel delivery.
stages.kit: Middle-height tee, regular bat, light one-hand bat, soft balls, net, non-slip floor.
stages.normalSwings: Same middle-tee setting throughout; prepare first, then record 6 uncued baseline swings.
stages.exit: Six normal two-hand swings, no technique cue. Look for a controlled load/landing and delivery without recovery; 4/6 is provisional progress, confirmed next session.
stages.next: If not ready: Shorten the load and stride; reduce effort. Use light dry rehearsals instead of one-hand ball contact if control is poor.

stages.name: Coil, Receive, Organize

blocks.run: Small coil, brief pause, controlled stride; dry rehearsal.
blocks.watch: Larger twist or sway requiring a foot/body correction.

blocks.run: Land, pause 1–2 seconds, then swing without another step.
blocks.watch: Knee folding plus a second forward pelvis surge.

blocks.run: 2 slow dry slot pauses + 2 continuous tee swings = 4 drill reps.
blocks.watch: Elbow/hand drop together with an unwanted barrel change and late correction.

focus.run: Fold arms or use short foam rod; slowly turn toward a middle-height target.
Small lead-foot taps into a gentle tee swing; avoid hopping.
Pre-set comfortable staggered base, gather and scoop without a stride; watch for sliding or recovery.

stages.goal: Carry a small loading turn into a controlled landing and arm delivery.
stages.kit: Middle-height tee, manageable bat, soft balls, net; folded arms or short foam rod for optional P.
stages.normalSwings: Same middle-tee setting; begin with 6 baseline/retention swings.
stages.exit: Six uncued normal swings with the pauses removed. Seek a smooth turn without a second surge or abrupt barrel correction; 4/6 plus next-session retention advances.
stages.next: If not ready: Return to Stage 1 or reduce pauses. Do not pin the elbow down, freeze the torso, or preserve a segmented rhythm in normal swings.

stages.name: Supported Turn, Controlled Reach

blocks.run: Arms folded; load, small stride, comfortable no-bat turn.
blocks.watch: Shoe twisting with wobble, slipping, or a recovery.

blocks.run: Tape a comfortable landing area; swing while allowing natural pivot.
blocks.watch: Abrupt heel sliding with loss of support, not normal rotation.

blocks.run: Small comfortable split grip, easy tee swings; restore normal grip.
blocks.watch: Early rear-arm straightening plus outward hand travel/wider approach.

focus.run: Easy no-stride tee swings; allow natural torso tilt.
Decelerate naturally, then hold a comfortable finish about 2 seconds.
Support ball near rear shoulder, turn and push-release; watch for an early reach followed by a body correction. Use #58 if uncomfortable.

stages.goal: Coordinate the turn without forced foot spinning or early reaching.
stages.cue: Turn through a comfortable, supported stance.
stages.kit: Middle-height tee, soft balls, net, flat tape, light bat with safe split-grip space.
stages.normalSwings: Same tee setting and regular grip; begin with 6 baseline/retention swings.
stages.exit: Six uncued normal swings. Seek supported feet and controlled delivery; 4/6 plus next-session retention advances.
stages.next: If not ready: Remove the constraint and lower effort. Do not glue either foot down or use a posed finish as proof of good pre-contact mechanics.

stages.name: Add Movement, Keep Control

blocks.run: Small rear-foot step toward catcher → smooth stride → easy tee swing.
blocks.watch: Hop or oversized step followed by a rushed landing.

blocks.run: 2 pairs: normal swing, safe reset, no-stride second swing. Both swings count.
blocks.watch: Second-rep knee folding with drift, or abrupt rising and recovery.

blocks.run: Two hands through contact; allow later top-hand release with secure bottom-hand control.
blocks.watch: Clearly pre-contact release or loss of bat control.

focus.run: Reachable low tee; smooth adjustment; restore middle tee for normal swings.
Modest lead-leg lift/lower into an easy tee swing; use dry reps if needed.
Small rearward step → gather → land → scoop; watch for a hop or rushed landing.

stages.goal: Introduce a small step-back while preserving landing and finish control.
stages.cue: Move smoothly into a balanced swing.
stages.kit: Middle-height tee, manageable bat, soft balls, net, clear space behind stance.
stages.normalSwings: Regular start and finish; begin with 6 baseline/retention swings.
stages.exit: Six uncued normal swings, without forced step-back or release. Seek control independent of the drill; 4/6 plus next-session retention advances.
stages.next: If not ready: Return to Stage 3; reduce movement. Do not force one-hand release or a high leg lift.

stages.name: Rhythm Meets a Moving Ball

blocks.run: 4 small-rock tee swings; then 4 normal toss swings.
blocks.watch: Extra sinking followed by a rise, or reaching while moving catcherward.

blocks.run: 4 dry strides under a virtual reference; then 4 normal toss swings.
blocks.watch: Abrupt head/pelvis rise or forward surge with control loss.

blocks.run: 4 gentle top-hand-only tosses; then 4 normal two-hand toss swings.
blocks.watch: Early reaching; review rollover only if hand orientation is clearly visible.

focus.run: Tee order middle → high → low → middle; then 4 normal toss swings.
4 no-swing tosses with location reports; then 4 normal toss swings.
Short walking approach → controlled landing → turn and scoop; watch for sliding or falling through release. Transfer to normal toss or the chosen tee version.

stages.goal: Preserve control with predictable gentle tosses.
stages.cue: Move smoothly and meet the ball.
stages.kit: Tee, regular/light one-hand bats, helmet, soft balls, net, protected consistent tosser; virtual height guide only.
stages.normalSwings: Start: Check Stage 4 retention with 6 tee swings; if advancing to toss, add a separate 6-toss baseline and log the extra set.
stages.exit: Six uncued normal toss swings matching the toss baseline. Seek controlled delivery on comparable feeds; 4/6 plus retention advances.
stages.next: If not ready: Improve the toss or stay on the tee. Do not force a still head, infer gaze from head pose, or score an errant feed as a mechanical failure.

stages.name: Integrate, Then Remove the Drills

blocks.run: 4 small-shuffle tee swings; then 4 normal swings.
blocks.watch: Hop, rushed landing, or stalled move followed by reaching.

blocks.run: 4 paused tee swings without a second surge; then 4 normal swings.
blocks.watch: Knee folding plus renewed forward travel.

blocks.run: 4 reachable deeper-tee swings; then 4 normal swings at baseline setup.
blocks.watch: Early reaching/withdrawal; do not diagnose from ball direction alone.

focus.run: Four comfortable, initially announced location changes; then 4 matched normal swings.
Four gentle swing/take deliveries with an agreed window; then 4 normal swings. Takes count as tasks.
Small non-crossing shuffle → gather → land → scoop; watch for tangled feet or recovery. Return to the matched normal-swing setup afterward.

stages.goal: Preserve normal-swing control after momentum and location tasks.
stages.cue: See it, move smoothly, and hit.
stages.kit: Tee, bat, helmet, soft balls, net, clear approach lane, protected consistent tosser if ready.
stages.normalSwings: One matched predictable toss setting, or tee-only version; begin with 6 baseline/retention swings.
stages.exit: Six uncued normal swings, without shuffle, pause, or deeper tee. Seek 4/6 controlled reps; confirm at a later matched normal-swing check before calling the progression retained.
stages.next: If ready: Optionally add six location-challenge swings if workload permits; log separately, never mix into the exit score. Otherwise stop and retain the simpler task.

decisions.text: Advance provisionally: Meet the chosen exit gate with safe control; confirm retention next session. Repeat or simplify: Comfortable but inconsistent, or constraints are not carrying over to normal swings.

Fix capture: Too few assessable reps, hidden landmarks, camera movement, or unclear feed location. Stop the task: Pain, slipping, unsafe bat control, or repeated loss of balance; do not chase a passing score with extra swings.

howToUse.label: Suggested cadence
howToUse.text: Use two skill sessions per week when compatible with the hitter's team practices, games, recovery, and other training. Six successful stages could occupy about three weeks, but repeating a stage is preferable to advancing on the calendar.

howToUse.label: Starting point
howToUse.text: Begin at Stage 1 unless a coach has already observed consistent control of the earlier tasks. Do not jump straight to momentum drills because a hitter can make hard contact.

howToUse.label: Session length
howToUse.text: Allow approximately 30–40 minutes, including preparation, equipment changes, rest, and video review. Treat this as a planning allowance rather than a performance target.

howToUse.label: Training dose
howToUse.text: The standard template contains 36 task repetitions: six baseline normal swings, twelve drill repetitions, twelve normal transfer swings, and six exit swings. Dry movements count as drill repetitions; warm-up movements and any later challenge swings are additional and must be logged separately.

howToUse.label: One cue at a time
howToUse.text: Each block has its own cue. During normal swings, use just the session's simple integration cue rather than asking the hitter to consciously control the rear knee, front knee, elbow, and wrists simultaneously.

howToUse.label: Separate drills, not a combined trick swing
howToUse.text: Do not combine a step-back start, forced front-leg finish, and one-hand release in the same rep. Complete each constraint on its own, then remove it for the normal transfer swings.

howToUse.label: Transfer is the goal
howToUse.text: Better execution of a drill does not automatically mean a better normal swing. Judge the baseline and exit swings under matched tee/toss conditions and review mechanical evidence separately from contact outcomes.

howToUse.label: Focus options
howToUse.text: Retain the original 36-task-rep session, or select ONE posture (P), balance/head-control (B), OR medicine-ball (M) block. Each adds four drill task reps and four normal transfer swings for 44 total task reps; it is optional, not a new minimum workload. For medicine balls, four reps means four throws total, not four per side.

equipment.label: Core kit
equipment.text: Adjustable tee, manageable regular bat, short/light one-hand bat or safely choked-up light bat, soft practice balls, net, flat floor tape, and a non-slip hitting area.

equipment.label: Video
equipment.text: Fixed camera showing the full body, both feet, and bat arc. Add a synchronized protected front/oblique view when possible; keep cameras and people outside the swing and ball paths.

equipment.label: Moving-ball work
equipment.text: Use a competent tosser and appropriate protection, with consistent, gentle delivery. If tosses or tracking are unreliable, retain the tee version instead of increasing difficulty.

equipment.label: Excluded from the standard progression
equipment.text: Raised platforms, rigid elbow/foot barriers, medicine-ball throws, and the advanced kneeling-rise drill remain unnecessary for the base plan. The separate M option below permits supervised medicine-ball work only with a suitable ball, approved target, clear lane, and controlled technique.

equipment.label: Safety
equipment.text: Begin at easy, controlled effort; never force a locked knee, heel-down position, inward knee drive, or abrupt full-speed bat stop. Stop for pain, slipping, or repeated loss of control, and do not resume progression by simply adding more reps.

structure.dose: Comfortable movement warm-up and a few easy dry swings; adjust to the hitter
structure.task: Confirm space, surface, bat control, and pain-free movement. Explain one session goal.
Use the stage's standard tee/toss setting with no special mechanical cue. These establish the comparison condition.
Rehearse the gather or movement transition, then remove the drill constraint.
Rehearse receiving the stride or supporting the turn, then restore the normal swing.
Rehearse arm/barrel delivery at manageable effort, then use a regular grip and finish.
Match the baseline setup, bat, pitch/tee location, and effort. Remove the technique cue for this check.

structure.dose: Brief comparison of baseline and exit clips
structure.task: Select one observation and decide: advance provisionally, repeat, simplify, or fix capture.

advancement.label: Controlled normal rep
advancement.text: The hitter completes the normal swing without a slip, unplanned recovery step, or other clear loss of control, and the chosen candidate flaw is absent or less pronounced relative to a coach-approved reference. Record contact quality separately; a hard hit alone does not qualify the mechanics.

advancement.label: Provisional advance
advancement.text: Aim for at least four controlled reps out of six assessable normal exit swings, with no pain, new safety issue, or material worsening from baseline. If baseline already meets the criterion, look for preserved control under the stage's task rather than forcing a numerical improvement.

advancement.label: Retention check
advancement.text: At the next session, use its first six normal baseline swings as a check of the prior stage. Begin under the prior stage's test condition before changing the feed; for the Stage 4→5 transition, do the retention check on the tee and add a separate six-toss baseline if proceeding, logging that extra set.

advancement.label: Confirmed advance
advancement.text: When the retention set also reaches the proposed four-of-six gate, proceed to the next stage. If retention fails, repeat or simplify the previous stage rather than adding a new constraint; Stage 6 also needs a later normal-swing check before calling the progression retained.

advancement.label: Repeat
advancement.text: If the exit set shows comfortable control but the target pattern remains inconsistent, keep the same stage at the next session. Do not simply double the volume.

advancement.label: Simplify
advancement.text: Remove one demand: shorten the load/step, reduce effort, switch moving ball to tee, return to two hands, or use a no-ball rehearsal. Do not compensate for poor one-hand control with a heavier bat or more forceful cues.

advancement.label: Capture failure
advancement.text: If fewer than six reps are assessable for the target, report “insufficient evidence,” retain the actual denominator, and fix camera position, light, or visibility. Do not count an occluded hand as a failed rollover rep or keep swinging indefinitely to fill a video quota.

advancement.label: Stop
advancement.text: Pain, a slipping surface, unsafe bat control, or repeated balance loss ends that task. Address the cause before resuming, and seek appropriate professional assessment for pain or injury concerns.

adjustments.situation: New hitter, limited attention, or tiring quickly
adjustments.adjustment: Use 4 baseline swings; 2 drill reps + 2 normal swings per block; 4 exit swings. This is 20 task reps plus warm-up.
adjustments.check: Proposed gate becomes 3 of 4 assessable controlled exit reps, with the same later retention check; label this the reduced-dose version.

adjustments.adjustment: Replace one-hand ball contact with light dry rehearsals, then normal two-hand swings; do not force the one-hand assignment.
adjustments.check: Evaluate ordinary two-hand delivery and control, not success at managing an unsuitable bat.

adjustments.situation: Tosser or moving-ball tracking is unavailable
adjustments.adjustment: Keep baseline, normal transfer, and exit on the same tee location.
adjustments.check: Record “tee transfer demonstrated”; do not claim moving-ball transfer.

adjustments.adjustment: Preserve the standard matched baseline/exit and add at most the planned optional location challenge when workload allows.
adjustments.check: Keep challenge performance separate from the baseline comparison and change one variable at a time.

substitutions.pattern: Sinking or rising during the load, with recovery
substitutions.upper: #1 One-Hand Top-Hand Tee, only if manageable
substitutions.caution: Look for coordinated knee/pelvis/head changes and actual control loss; do not eliminate normal knee bend.

substitutions.rear: #24 Step-Back Tee Swings at very small scale, or #22 if movement is too difficult
substitutions.caution: Review the landing and continued pelvis travel together; do not use a fixed knee angle or require the body to be motionless.

substitutions.pattern: Rear-foot slipping or deliberate shoe twisting
substitutions.caution: Review foot translation/rotation with body control. Natural pivoting and heel lift remain permitted.

substitutions.pattern: Persistent elbow-ahead pattern with delayed barrel delivery
substitutions.upper: #10 Rear-Elbow Path Video Check, virtual overlay only
substitutions.caution: Confirm elbow–grip timing and barrel delivery across views. The lower-body pairing supplies context, not proof of causation.

substitutions.pattern: Visible hand turnover before contact on similar pitches
substitutions.rear: #25 Wide-Stance Rocker Swings at easy effort
substitutions.upper: #2 Top-Hand Soft Toss or #11 Opposite-Field Deep Tee
substitutions.caution: Require usable hand evidence; wrist crossover and ball direction alone cannot establish rollover.

substitutions.pattern: Loss of control when adding motion
substitutions.rear: #22 Rear-Hip Hinge Pause instead of shuffle/step-back
substitutions.upper: #1 One-Hand Top-Hand Tee or a controlled two-hand tee round
substitutions.caution: Return to the simpler setup before adding speed, momentum, or a moving ball.

focusAlternatives.label: Posture foundations
focusAlternatives.text: #44 Torso Path Video Check can replace #34 when video feedback is more useful than a held landing; #36 Slow Delivery-Path Rehearsal can replace #35 for a slow bat-path rehearsal.

focusAlternatives.label: Posture constraints
focusAlternatives.text: #42 Short-Bat Posture Swings can replace #37 only with a suitable manageable implement. #41 Low-Outside Tee Reach can replace #38 after confirming the tee is safely reachable.

focusAlternatives.label: Posture variation
focusAlternatives.text: #39 High-Tee Posture Swings can replace #40 when one height needs work before mixing heights. #43 Three-Stance Rotation Check can replace #45 as four reps: open, regular no-stride, closed, regular no-stride, with small comfortable stance changes.

focusAlternatives.label: Head/balance foundations
focusAlternatives.text: #54 Slow-Motion Head-Path Review can replace #46 for slow video feedback; #48 Feet-Together Stride Swings can replace #47 if taps are confusing.

focusAlternatives.label: Finish and attention
focusAlternatives.text: #51 Contact-to-Finish Rehearsal can replace #50 when a gentle partial rehearsal is more manageable. #52 Tee-Top Focus Swings can replace #49 if the need is attention/head awareness rather than a harder leg-lift task.

focusAlternatives.label: Recognition
focusAlternatives.text: #56 Color-Call Takes can replace #55 when markings are clearly visible; use four no-swing takes, not four hits. #53 Post-Swing Symbol Call can replace #57 as a low-effort tee attention task, but is not equivalent evidence of pitch decisions.

focusAlternatives.label: Avoid unsafe shortcuts
focusAlternatives.text: Do not add head restraints, shirt biting, eyes-closed swings, wobble-board hitting, or a coach's hand near contact. An attention drill that creates neck stiffness or diving should be removed rather than intensified.

medicineBall.label: Equipment gate
medicineBall.text: A qualified coach selects a known, manageable ball and verifies the wall or landing area is appropriate. Use a clear non-slip lane, keep people and cameras out of the rebound path, and do not assume a batting net will safely stop a medicine ball.

medicineBall.label: Rehearse first
medicineBall.text: Perform a comfortable no-ball walkthrough as needed and log those extra reps. Throwing safely is a separate readiness decision from passing the hitting stage; an athlete can remain on #58 throughout the progression.

medicineBall.label: Four total, not per side
medicineBall.text: Use four discrete medicine-ball reps, normally two per comfortable direction when appropriate, with full resets. If the coach uses one direction only, still total four and record the choice; the reduced mode uses two total reps, not two per side.

medicineBall.label: Normal transfer
medicineBall.text: After the ball is safely stopped and the lane cleared, rest as needed and take four normal two-hand swings under the session's baseline condition. The M block contains no bat–medicine-ball contact and no simultaneous swinging/throwing.

medicineBall.label: Same session totals
medicineBall.text: Base = 36, selected M = 44; reduced base = 20, reduced M = 24. Warm-up/rehearsals, extra transition baselines, or challenge reps are additional; do not add a separate bilateral set without logging and adjusting workload.

medicineBall.label: No rebound catching
medicineBall.text: Wait until the ball stops before retrieval. Omit rapid partner exchanges, run-up competitions, and maximum-load attempts from these coach cards.

medicineBall.label: Simplify
medicineBall.text: Use #30 or #58 in any stage, use a lighter ball, or return to no-ball rehearsal. Never solve poor control by adding weight, effort, or extra throws.

medicineBall.label: Kneeling alternatives
medicineBall.text: #64, #65, and #67 can replace a selected medicine-ball task only if a coach finds the position comfortable and suitable. They change the task; do not claim they isolate a muscle or preserve the standing phase sequence.

medicineBall.label: Advanced option
medicineBall.text: #63 Step-Behind Rotational Push Throw is optional supervised work after simpler footwork is reliable, not an automatic next step or a required Stage 6 upgrade.

medicineBall.label: Supplemental options
medicineBall.text: #68 Controlled Overhead Floor Slam and #69 Medicine-Ball Carry and Place may replace the M task for a separately identified general movement goal. They are not equivalent tests of rotational hitting or excuses to stack more reps.

medicineBall.label: Advance separately
medicineBall.text: The hitting plan still uses the normal-swing exit/retention gate. A good throw does not count as a controlled normal swing; readiness for a more complex medicine-ball task is a separate coach decision with ball, direction, target, and effort held comparable.

medicineBall.label: Do not infer power
medicineBall.text: Log visible control, release/placement timing, target result, and any recovery. Label ball mass from verified metadata and report speed only with appropriate calibration; do not calculate a force, torque, gaze, or bat-speed score from pose alone.

limitations: The drills adapt common coaching drill families. Outside organisations’ names and links were removed at the founder’s request (2026-11-02), and every drill was given a generic Base Recruits name.

Nothing in this workbook is presented as a sourced fact. Instructions, rep counts, pairings, the six-stage order and the 4-of-6 advancement rule are coaching proposals, not validated biomechanical or age-specific standards.
The AI-analysis fields are proposed review rules for video, not a validated computer-vision system. Body pose cannot measure eye gaze, force, foot pressure or muscle activation.
The hitter’s age, training history, injury history and current workload are not known to the workbook. A coach scales the plan before use and makes every advancement decision.

Medicine-ball work needs a coach-selected ball of known, manageable mass, an approved wall or landing area, a clear lane and discrete throws. No rebound catching, no universal ball weight and no power score.
Stop any task for pain, slipping, unsafe bat control or repeated loss of balance, and seek appropriate professional advice for pain or injury concerns.
